reply.summary: Research artifact written to docs/designs/006-self-update-checkpoint-compatibility/01-research.md, organized around ADR-006's three questions. Key findings: cross-version compatibility today is only the additive-optional field discipline plus one backfill, with a hard-rejected literal version 1 and no migration mechanism; the worktree checkpoint sits inside every document/review stage's write-set while the committed copy is already the de facto recovery anchor (git checkout HEAD hint, save-before-commit); and when the checkpoint can't be written, the escalation record dies with it since finalizeEscalate writes through the failing save path. Prior art covers Terraform state compatibility/locking, Step Functions immutable versions, Temporal replay versioning, SQLite journal-marker recovery, POSIX rename and Node fs primitives, plus the run-2 postmortem read from git history; the check-then-write lockfile and checkpoint-to-prompt findings re-injection are flagged under the security lens. Applied lenses: Prior art, Security landscape, Platform notes. All internal citations verified against current file line numbers; external quotes re-fetched and verified.
reply.commitMessage: docs: add research for ADR-006 self-update checkpoint compatibility

findings.location: §1 Fence runner-reserved paths in the ownership matrix — "return `false` when the path's last segment is `STATE_FILE` (`.pipeline.json`), starts with `${STATE_FILE}.`"
findings.problem: new — The last-segment rule is an exact-string match with no case normalization. On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS is listed `yes` in the Compatibility matrix), a stage writing `.Pipeline.json`/`.PIPELINE.JSON` passes the string rule while hitting the same on-disk file the fence exists to protect, so the Goals claim that the copies "can only carry runner-authored bytes" is not guaranteed on a supported platform.
findings.fix: Make the reserved-name comparison case-insensitive when the underlying filesystem is case-insensitive (practically: on `darwin`/`win32`) in the same §1 sentence, and add one note to the macOS row of the Compatibility matrix that the fence rule is case-folded there. This qualifies the existing rule; it introduces no new mechanism.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Node `>= 22.23.4` (engine floor)"
findings.problem: new — Advisory check (checklist item 5): 22.23.4 is itself the fixed release for CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli RCE, High), and Node has pre-alerted another 22.x security release for 2026-11-11 (highest severity High, details not yet public). Because the design states a floor (`>=`), not a pin, no unfixed advisory is forced on the design — informational only.
findings.fix: One sentence in the matrix row: the floor is a minimum; operators run the newest patched 22.x (the 2026-11-11 security release once it lands).

findings.location: §3 An escalation that survives its own failing write — "prints the repair commands — `git checkout HEAD -- <designDir>/.pipeline.json`, ... `rm -r <designDir>/.pipeline.json && git checkout HEAD -- …`"
findings.problem: new — Path-interpolated command strings the operator copy-pastes; an unquoted path mis-tokenizes in a shell. The commands are printed, never executed by the runner, so this is exposure via operator copy-paste only (run slugs are conventionally simple).
findings.fix: Specify the printed commands with the interpolated paths single-quoted.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Windows | unknown | No CI workflow exists to exercise it"
findings.problem: Checklist item 1: an `unknown` status must appear as a finding. The matrix is the document's compatibility contract, and an `unknown` cell ships an undecided answer while the design makes Windows-differing primitives (rename, 'wx', the §3 repair commands) load-bearing, so operators get no Windows posture from the document that decides this. Not a reopening of the Deferred item (deferring the CI work is ADR-consistent); the status column must still record a decision.
findings.fix: Change the cell to an explicit status — e.g. `no (unverified)` — keeping the existing note text; only the status cell changes. A later dated Windows smoke job may flip it to `yes`.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix / Test strategy (Platform) — "macOS | yes | POSIX semantics hold; not exercised by CI in this repo" and "the macOS, Windows, and network-FS rows are not exercised by this run"
findings.problem: Checklist item 7: the Test strategy must name a platform test for every platform the matrix claims as supported. macOS is claimed `yes` but no named test run covers it; the POSIX-parity claim rests on documentation (A5/A6), not an exercised check.
findings.fix: Add one Platform-paragraph line naming a concrete macOS run of the existing suites (a dated manual/dev-machine run satisfies item 7 without CI), or demote the macOS row to the `partial` status the network row already uses.

findings.location: Test strategy (Platform) vs Assumption register A12 — "Linux CI exercises all of the above" vs A12 "nothing in this repo exercises it (no CI workflow found)"
findings.problem: The document contradicts itself about whether a CI runner exists. If none exists, "Linux CI" names a non-existent artifact and the Linux platform-test claim has no named runner; if one exists, A12's basis is stale.
findings.fix: Replace "Linux CI exercises all of the above" with the actual runner — "the existing `tools/orchestration` test suite, run on Linux" — or add a Linux CI workflow as a named Rollout deliverable and correct A12.

findings.location: §1 Fence — "return `false` when the path's last segment is `STATE_FILE` (`.pipeline.json`), starts with `${STATE_FILE}.`"
findings.problem: The rule never states how the last segment is derived or how case is compared (checklist item 6: separators and case handled by a library). On a case-insensitive filesystem — macOS is claimed `yes` — a write reported as `.PIPELINE.JSON` passes an exact-string fence while the filesystem routes it to the checkpoint's file, breaking §1's "neither copy can ever again carry model-authored bytes"; naive splitting also misparses Windows path shapes.
findings.fix: One sentence binding the matcher to path-library semantics — `path.basename` comparison, case-insensitive comparison on case-insensitive platforms — reusing the moves validator's existing normalization (moves.ts:107–131) instead of new string logic.

findings.location: §3 finalizeEscalate — "prints the repair commands — `git checkout HEAD -- <designDir>/.pipeline.json`"
findings.problem: The printed repair commands (including the `rm -r …` variant) are POSIX-shell only — consistent while Windows is undecided, but unusable if Windows ever becomes a support claim.
findings.fix: Conditional: if the Windows row becomes a support claim, name the PowerShell equivalents of the repair commands alongside the POSIX ones.

findings.location: §3 An escalation that survives its own failing write — "`resumePipeline` (`runner.ts:1983–1989`) writes a `gateLog` entry (`terminalSaveFailed`, reason quoting the marker's failure line) before deleting the marker"
findings.problem: new: the design adds a writer to a persisted, append-only array on the escalate → repair → resume cycle without stating whether `gateLog` is bounded, while §2 explicitly names the bound for the neighboring field ("`stageCommits` keeps its bounded-window meaning … as named contract, not comment"). This design's subject is checkpoints that outlive the run that wrote them and that operators repair and resume repeatedly, and `gateLog` is re-parsed by `loadState` on every resume, re-serialized on every save, and scanned by the escalation report (A4: "escalationMarkdown renders the last denied gate-log entries from the in-memory state"), so an unbounded growth path there is exactly the memory-growth question the checklist asks; the silence reads as unexamined rather than deliberate.
findings.fix: Extend the §2 contract bullet (or add one clause to §3's split-record bullet) naming the `gateLog` growth limit the same way — "windowed like `stageCommits`" or "append-only, bounded by the run's stage-and-attempt count, at the byte size the golden fixtures pin" — replacing the silence with a named-contract sentence rather than adding a trimming mechanism.

findings.location: §1 Fence runner-reserved paths / §3 split record / §4 Atomic lock acquisition — "gains a first rule that precedes the per-stage rules", "checks for the marker alongside the loaded state", "on `EEXIST`, read the holder and apply today's pid-liveness logic unchanged"
findings.problem: new: the design adds three new per-operation costs (a segment test per swept path, one extra stat per `pipeline status` call plus one extra read per resume, one extra read and one `'wx'` retry per contended lock acquire) and states no cost expectation for any of them; no baseline, number, or performance statement appears anywhere in the document, so a reader cannot tell whether "these are free" was reasoned about or assumed. The research baseline could not be quoted in this seat (not among its inputs), so the checklist's baseline-vs-expectation comparison has nothing to compare against in the text.
findings.fix: One sentence at the head of Risks or end of §4: "the fence is a constant-time segment check added to the existing per-path sweep; the split-record check is one `stat` per `status` call and one read per resume; the lock path gains one read and one retry only under contention; nothing here is on a per-event path, so no runtime budget applies" — plus a citation to the research document's checkpoint size/load baseline if it carries one.

findings.location: Chosen design §1 Fence runner-reserved paths in the ownership matrix — Q2 — "starts with `${STATE_FILE}.` (the saveState tmp pattern, `state-store.ts:186`)"
findings.problem: The tmp-name convention is minted in saveState (state-store.ts:186) but the fence re-derives it inline in gates.ts as a hard-coded prefix rule. The design's 'share one vocabulary' move exports the reserved names to types.ts yet leaves the reserved pattern duplicated across two files, so a future change to the tmp scheme in state-store.ts silently desynchronizes the fence's second rule.
findings.fix: Export the pattern from state-store.ts where it is minted (a small predicate such as isStateTmpSegment, or the tmp base-name constant) and have gates.ts consume it instead of rebuilding the prefix inline — the same single-vocabulary move the design already makes for STATE_FILE/ESCALATION.md.

findings.location: Chosen design §2 The cross-version resume contract — Q1 — "Canonical statement, written into the `StateSchema` header in `state-store.ts` and into `docs/workflows.md` for operators"
findings.problem: The full rule set is written verbatim in two places and nothing in the Test strategy pins the two copies together, so the operator-facing doc can silently drift from the contract the golden fixtures enforce.
findings.fix: Keep the full contract in one home (the StateSchema header, where the engineer adding a field reads it) and let docs/workflows.md carry only the operator-facing subset (refusal message, recovery postures) with a pointer to the header — reducing rather than adding duplicated text.

findings.location: §1 Chosen design "Fence runner-reserved paths in the ownership matrix" — "`stagePathAllowed(stage, path)` (`gates.ts:260–273`) gains a first rule that precedes the per-stage rules: return `false` when the path's last segment is `STATE_FILE`"
findings.problem: new — The fence lands in the same author-agnostic predicate enforceOwnership uses for its violation set (runner.ts:260–261: own-commit paths + dirtyFiles), which is A3's own cited basis. At every boundary sweep the checkpoint is dirty by the runner's own save (pass writes drain before the sweep at runner.ts:1871; checkpoint() re-saves after the commit at runner.ts:2298, 2336), so the sweep reverts or deletes the runner's own checkpoint writes: mid-run boundary commits never advance the committed copy (contradicting A7's `verified` "newest good state at every stage boundary"); a new run's untracked checkpoint is deleted at the first sweep and never committed until terminal, so §3's `git checkout HEAD --` repair, the loadState message, and Test #13 reference a path absent from HEAD; and resume's ESCALATION.md deletion (runner.ts:1983–1989) is restored at the next sweep, making the split-record line misfire. Test #2's "byte-identical to headBefore" assertion is exactly the misfire output, so no listed test catches it.
findings.fix: Keep the stagePathAllowed rule for attribution/reporting, but replace §1's third-bullet behavior ("the sweep restores the file from `headBefore` and removes the planted tree") with a reserved-name branch in the sweep: restore the path to the runner's authoritative content — re-save from the in-memory PipelineState via checkpoint() for .pipeline.json, re-apply resume's deletion for ESCALATION.md — instead of headBefore restore or removal.

findings.location: §2 cross-version resume contract — "name the operator's two postures — resume with the pipeline that wrote it, or start a fresh run after archiving the run directory (ADR-006:55–57)"
findings.problem: new — The cited ADR lines give a different pair: "`git checkout HEAD -- docs/designs/<run>/.pipeline.json` or a fresh run". The quoted first posture appears nowhere in the ADR and the ADR's first posture is missing from the pair; the refusal message and docs/workflows.md inherit an unsupported attribution.
findings.fix: Cite ADR-006:55–57 only as the precedent for naming operator postures in an error, and present the refusal pair as this design's own addition, or restate the pair to match the ADR's.

findings.location: §1 — "starts with `${STATE_FILE}.` (the `saveState` tmp pattern, `state-store.ts:186`)"
findings.problem: new — The prefix rule fences any name beginning `.pipeline.json.` at any depth, so a legitimate doc file such as `.pipeline.json-notes.md` can never be written by a stage.
findings.fix: Either state the breadth is deliberate and pin Test #1 on a neighboring name being forbidden, or match the tmp shape exactly (`/^\.pipeline\.json\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.tmp$/` on the last segment).

reply.summary: Blocker (§1 fence): the sweep is author-agnostic, so the reserved-name rule is no longer a bare name test — `enforceOwnership` now skips a touched reserved path while it still holds the bytes `saveState` last wrote (or is absent because the runner deleted it), which restores A7, the first boundary commit of a new run's untracked checkpoint, and resume's `ESCALATION.md` deletion; Test #2 was rewritten to pin both directions instead of asserting byte-identity with `headBefore`. Compat majors: the Windows cell is now `no (unverified)` with a note limited to what A12 supports, and macOS is demoted to `partial` since no named run covers it. Compat minors: the Platform paragraph names the `tools/orchestration` suite on Linux (matching A12's no-CI basis, now marked verified) instead of a non-existent Linux CI, and the fence matcher is bound to segment-wise, case-insensitive comparison reusing moves.ts:134–147. Correctness minor/nit: §2's refusal now quotes the ADR's actual postures (restore the committed copy, or a fresh run), and the tmp rule matches the exact `.pipeline.json.<8 hex>.tmp` shape with Test #1 pinning `.pipeline.json-notes.md` as allowed. Offsetting deletions: the duplicated auto-reconcile option and the Non-goals/Deferred repeats were consolidated into Deferred, the schema-change paragraph at the end of §4 was removed, and §2/§3 prose was tightened — net −1 line overall.

findings.location: §1 Fence — "compared segment-by-segment and case-insensitively the way the moves validator already compares these names (`moves.ts:134–147`)"
findings.problem: new — the cited precedent compares these very names case-sensitively: moves.ts:136 is `segment === STATE_FILE` and :139 `segment === LOCK_FILE`; the only case-folded comparison in that block is `segment.toLowerCase() === '.git'` (line 142). The sentence binds the fence's case handling to code that does the opposite for exactly STATE_FILE/LOCK_FILE, so an implementer who follows the cited precedent builds a case-sensitive fence and fails Test #1's `.PIPELINE.JSON` case — the gap this revision was written to close.
findings.fix: Keep the behavior sentence and re-anchor the precedent: "following the `segment.toLowerCase() === '.git'` pattern at moves.ts:142, widening the existing `segment === STATE_FILE` comparison at moves.ts:136 rather than copying it", and state the fold applies on every platform, so on case-sensitive Linux it deliberately over-matches `.Pipeline.json` (Test #1 already pins that).

findings.location: FYI — §2 May refuse — "restore the committed copy (`git checkout HEAD -- …`) or start a fresh run (ADR-006:55–57)"
findings.problem: not a compatibility finding; noted for the correctness seat. This is now verbatim the ADR's interim posture, which is right for the schema-rejection half of the bullet but cannot help the unknown-`version` half: the committed copy carries the same version as the worktree copy.
findings.fix: If the correctness seat agrees, let the refusal message differ per refusal cause: committed-copy restore for a rejected shape, resume-with-the-writing-pipeline / fresh run for an unknown version.

findings.location: §1 Fence — "compared segment-by-segment and case-insensitively the way the moves validator already compares these names (`moves.ts:134–147`)"
findings.problem: new — The cited validator compares STATE_FILE/LOCK_FILE segments with plain `===` (case-sensitive, moves.ts:136, 139); only `.git` uses `toLowerCase()` (moves.ts:142). The claimed existing precedent for case-insensitive comparison of the reserved names is false, and the revision log entry repeats the same mis-citation. The case-insensitive choice itself is sound (Test #1 pins `.PIPELINE.JSON`), but since Non-goals keep moves.ts:134–147 unchanged, the sentence implies a shared precedent that does not exist.
findings.fix: Reword to attribute case-insensitivity to this design: "segment-wise like the moves validator (`moves.ts:134–147`), with case-insensitivity added here (the validator's only case-insensitive name is `.git`, moves.ts:142)"; correct the matching r1 revision-log entry.

findings.location: §1 Fence consequences — "A stage write to the checkpoint is a content mismatch, reverted before that stage's `git add -A`" + "a new run's untracked checkpoint is committed by its first `commitStage`"
findings.problem: new — For a new run before its first `commitStage`, the checkpoint is absent from `headBefore`, and the cited revert mechanics (runner.ts:263–276) remove violations not present in `headBefore`: a tampered, untracked checkpoint is deleted outright — no copy in HEAD or worktree until the next `checkpoint()` (runner.ts:2336) re-saves from memory, and a crash in that window leaves nothing for §3's `git checkout HEAD --` repair to restore. The unconditional first-commit claim is false in exactly the tamper case the fence targets.
findings.fix: Extend the §1 authorship branch: a reserved-name match with a content mismatch that is absent from `headBefore` is re-saved from the in-memory PipelineState via `checkpoint()`, instead of the restore-or-remove branch of runner.ts:263–276; add the case to Test #2.

findings.location: §1 Fence runner-reserved paths in the ownership matrix — "a match is skipped while it still holds the bytes `saveState` last wrote for it, kept in memory (or is absent because the runner deleted it), and reverted otherwise"
findings.problem: new — the absence branch states a cause ("because the runner deleted it") but not the test that establishes it. Read as "absent ⇒ skip", a stage that deletes `.pipeline.json` (its write set covers `docs/**`, A1) escapes the revert and the next `commitStage` commits the deletion; after that the §3 repair the design prints, `git checkout HEAD -- <designDir>/.pipeline.json`, restores nothing because HEAD now records the deletion, so the committed recovery anchor (A7; ADR-006:55–57) is destroyed by a model-authored action. Same shape for a stage deleting the `ESCALATION.md` marker, which §3's split-record `status` check and `resumePipeline`'s gate-log entry both depend on. The text I approved in r1 restored unconditionally ("the sweep restores the file from `headBefore`"), so this is introduced by the revision, and Test strategy #2 pins planted edit/tmp/directory-replacement and the runner's own save but no stage-side deletion.
findings.fix: In the same sentence, make the skip require a recorded authorship by this process (its last `saveState` snapshot, or a delete this process itself performed) and state that every other state — including absence it did not author — is restored from `headBefore`; add one Test #2 case: a stage-deleted `.pipeline.json` and a stage-deleted `ESCALATION.md` are both restored. Qualifies the existing predicate; no new mechanism.

findings.location: §1 Fence (authorship test) vs §3 escalation — "the bytes `saveState` last wrote for it"
findings.problem: new — the exemption is keyed only to `saveState` snapshots and runner deletes, so the runner's own `ESCALATION.md` write is not exempt: §1 says the sweep filters "every touched path, runner saves included", and `finalizeEscalate` writes `ESCALATION.md` then "still runs `commitStage`". Under the exemption as written, that marker is a reserved match holding nothing `saveState` wrote, so it is reverted and the terminal record never lands — contradicting §3's guarantee (ADR-006 question 3) and Test #7's assertion that `ESCALATION.md` is written with no error escaping, and unmaking the `status` split-record line.
findings.fix: Generalize the exempted set in that clause to "bytes this process last wrote at that path — the `saveState` snapshot for the checkpoint, the escalation report writer's bytes for `ESCALATION.md`", i.e. make the Revision log's intent ("skips what the runner itself wrote in-window") operative; this replaces the saveState-only wording rather than adding a mechanism.

findings.location: §3 An escalation that survives its own failing write — "prints the repair commands — `git checkout HEAD -- <designDir>/.pipeline.json`, with the `rm -r <designDir>/.pipeline.json && git checkout HEAD -- …` variant"
findings.problem: re-raised — unchanged from r1: interpolated paths are printed unquoted, so a run slug containing a space or shell metacharacter mis-tokenizes when the operator copy-pastes (checklist item 3; exposure via copy-paste only, the runner never executes them). The §2 revision widens the pattern with one more printed string — "restore the committed copy (`git checkout HEAD -- …`)" — so the quoting rule is now better stated once than per site.
findings.fix: Specify the printed commands with the interpolated paths single-quoted, and let Test #5 (which already asserts the message names the `rm -r` + `git checkout HEAD --` repair) assert the quoted form.

reply.commitMessage: docs: language-only edit pass on ADR-006 checkpoint proposal
feat(orchestration): fence runner-reserved checkpoint paths, guard checkpoint saves, harden run lock, state the cross-version resume contract
fix(orchestration): sort runner.ts import specifiers to clear the prettier gate
test(orchestration): repair ADR-006 resume fixtures and pin the resume promise, not the funnel

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:2738–2745
findings.problem: finalizeEscalate writes ESCALATION.md with an unguarded bare writeFileSync. A stage that plants a file under a directory named ESCALATION.md in the design dir gets the inner file reverted by the sweep, but the then-empty untracked directory is invisible to git status (file-only with --untracked-files=all) and survives; the next escalation's marker write hits EISDIR, which is not a CheckpointWriteFailure, so it escapes the drive-loop branch (or the try entirely for decideNext escalations) and the run crashes with no terminal record, no commit, and status stuck running — the run-2 blocker §3 exists to close, reachable via the marker path because ESCALATION.md is untracked at first escalation and no directory-clear (as restoreCommittedCheckpoint does for the checkpoint) covers it.
findings.fix: Before writing the marker, clear a directory occupying reportRel using the existing existsSync(abs) && statSync(abs).isDirectory() → rmSync(abs,{recursive:true,force:true}) pattern from restoreCommittedCheckpoint, and wrap the marker write in try/catch that prints the full report to stderr as a fallback record. Add a regression test: plant ESCALATION.md/<file>, pass a stage boundary, force escalation, assert ESCALATION.md exists and no error escapes.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:2722–2724,2744
findings.problem: The comment claims the ESCALATION.md write is 'Atomic tmp+rename, like every other checkpoint write', but line 2744 is a direct writeFileSync; a crash mid-write truncates the one terminal marker §3 defines as the journal-equivalent, and resumePipeline's failure-line extraction then reads a partial record.
findings.fix: Write the marker through a tmp+rename pair (same shape as saveState) and align the comment with the code.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:2124–2127,2669
findings.problem: finalizeDone's checkpoint() call sits outside the drive loop's try (which starts at 2195), so a checkpoint unwritable at the completion boundary (directory-replacement class) raises a raw CheckpointWriteFailure that escapes runPipeline/resumePipeline: the done record and its commit never land and the CLI gets a crash — the same hostile-input class §3 converts to an escalation with a repair everywhere else.
findings.fix: Guard finalizeDone's save with the same CheckpointWriteFailure branch: on failure restore the committed checkpoint and escalate (or at minimum print the §3 repair commands) instead of throwing.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/types.ts:190–202
findings.problem: namesReservedSegment omits LOCK_FILE, so stagePathAllowed admits .pipeline.lock to implement/fix stages, and the lock is gitignored (.gitignore:3) so the ownership sweep structurally cannot see or restore it. A stage can delete or rewrite the lock, breaking the single-flight premise §1's trust posture leans on (§4's own goal: 'the runner is the only writer' holds across processes): the next acquireLock admits a second writer, or a planted live-pid holder blocks resume. The moves validator already names LOCK_FILE reserved (moves.ts:139–141), so the ownership-fence exclusion looks like an oversight.
findings.fix: Add LOCK_FILE to the reserved-segment set, and re-assert the lock at stage boundaries: if the lock file is absent or no longer names this pid/stage, recreate it with the 'wx' path before continuing (distinct from the Deferred lock-ID nonce).

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/state-store.ts:133–137
findings.problem: loadState reads the raw checkpoint without a size bound before JSON.parse. The security checklist's untrusted-file rule is 'schema-validated, size-limited', and the committed copy stays the recovery anchor for pre-fence history the design's own Risks row admits can carry model-authored bytes, so a multi-MB hostile checkpoint makes resume/status allocate unbounded memory before the schema rejects it.
findings.fix: Stat the file (or read a bounded prefix) and refuse oversize checkpoints with a message in the existing recovery-posture style before parsing.

results.failure: independence violation: read a review report: docs/designs/006-self-update-checkpoint-compatibility/reviews/code/*

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/types.ts:181 (with tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/state-store.ts:277)
findings.problem: The fence's tmp-shape matcher STATE_TMP_RE hard-codes the checkpoint literal, the 8-hex suffix width and '.tmp' as a second, independent copy of the naming rule that lives in saveState (`${target}.${randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}.tmp`). Nothing links them: if the writer's tmp name ever changes, saveState keeps working while the fence silently stops matching the runner's own tmp files, so stray checkpoint tmps reach `git add -A` instead of being swept. Tests cannot catch the drift because ownership.test.ts:245 plants a hand-written 8-hex name that matches the literal regardless of what saveState writes.
findings.fix: Define the shape once: export a stateTmpName(target) helper from state-store.ts, or build STATE_TMP_RE from STATE_FILE, and add a case that takes a tmp name actually produced by saveState and asserts namesReservedSegment denies it.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/state-store.ts:149 and state-store.ts:293 (consumed at runner.ts:2445 and runner.ts:2743)
findings.problem: The loadState and CheckpointWriteFailure repair messages interpolate `file`/`target`, which are absolute whenever the runner passes an absolute design dir (it always does). That text is not only printed: it becomes the escalation reason persisted in the gate log and re-saved by the next resume, and it is appended verbatim to ESCALATION.md. The run's terminal record therefore carries one machine's worktree path — the run-3-live fixture (line 408) shows exactly this shape — while ADR-006's own scenario is a resume after a self-update, possibly in a different worktree. finalizeEscalate already formats the same repair repo-relative (runner.ts:2758-2763), so the store-side messages are the inconsistent half.
findings.fix: Keep the path structured rather than pre-formatted: put `path` on CheckpointWriteFailure, render loadState's message from the design-dir-relative form, and let the printers emit repo-relative commands as runner.ts:2761 already does.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline/runner.test.ts:392-403 (claim at runner.ts:423 and the proposal's Compatibility matrix network-FS row)
findings.problem: Test #10's concurrency case does not exercise the platform claim §4 makes. acquireLock is fully synchronous, so Promise.all of two in-process calls simply serializes; the test passes unchanged against the deleted existsSync+writeFileSync code and pins nothing about 'wx'. The real local-FS window is still open and untested: a contender that reads the lock between the exclusive create and the write gets an empty file, holderOf() returns null, the code warns and unlinkSyncs the live holder's lock, then re-creates — two winners on a local filesystem, while the matrix attributes all residual risk to network/shared filesystems.
findings.fix: Make #10's third case contend two real processes (spawn/execFileSync of process.execPath running acquireLock against the same fixture repo) and assert exactly one succeeds; and either narrow the docstring/matrix claim to the create itself or state the empty/unparseable-lock window alongside the deferred lock-ID nonce.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/types.ts:183-189 (precedent cited at moves.ts:136-142; matrix macOS row)
findings.problem: The code comment (and the proposal's §1 citation) claims the reserved-name comparison is case-insensitive 'the way the moves validator already compares these names'. moves.ts compares STATE_FILE and LOCK_FILE case-sensitively — only .git is lower-cased. findings.location: §1 Fence consequences — "A stage write to the checkpoint is a content mismatch, reverted before that stage's `git add -A`" + "a new run's untracked checkpoint is committed by its first `commitStage`"

findings.location: §1 Fence — "compared segment-by-segment and case-insensitively the way the moves validator already compares these names (`moves.ts:134–147`)"

findings.location: §1 Fence runner-reserved paths in the ownership matrix — "a match is skipped while it still holds the bytes `saveState` last wrote for it, kept in memory (or is absent because the runner deleted it), and reverted otherwise"
findings.problem: new — the absence branch states a cause ("because the runner deleted it") but not the test that establishes it. Read as "absent ⇒ skip", a stage that deletes `.pipeline.json` (its write set covers `docs/**`, A1) escapes the revert and the next `commitStage` commits the deletion; after that the §3 repair the design prints, `git checkout HEAD -- <designDir>/.pipeline.json`, restores nothing because HEAD now records the deletion, so the committed recovery anchor (A7; ADR-006:55–57) is destroyed by a model-authored action. Same shape for a stage deleting the `ESCALATION.md` marker, which §3's split-record `status` check and `resumePipeline`'s gate-log entry both depend on. The text I approved in r1 restored unconditionally ("the sweep restores the file from `headBefore`"), so this is introduced by the revision, and Test strategy #2 pins planted edit/tmp/directory-replacement and the runner's own save but no stage-side deletion.
findings.fix: In the same sentence, make the skip require a recorded authorship by this process (its last `saveState` snapshot, or a delete this process itself performed) and state that every other state — including absence it did not author — is restored from `headBefore`; add one Test #2 case: a stage-deleted `.pipeline.json` and a stage-deleted `ESCALATION.md` are both restored. Qualifies the existing predicate; no new mechanism.

findings.location: §1 Fence (authorship test) vs §3 escalation — "the bytes `saveState` last wrote for it"

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/state-store.ts:263-313 (holdsRunnerBytes recorded-delete precedence added in 640c289)
findings.problem: A recorded delete outranks a recorded write permanently: recordRunnerWrite never clears runnerDeleted. If the runner deletes a reserved path and later rewrites it in the same process (resume's marker delete at runner.ts:2192, then a re-escalation's marker write at runner.ts:2884), holdsRunnerBytes returns false even though the file holds exactly the runner's fresh bytes, so any later sweep would revert the runner's own write. Latent only today — no ownership sweep runs between those two actions before finalizeEscalate's commitStage — but the pair is a state machine with a stranded delete flag.
findings.fix: Make the authorship records last-action-wins: recordRunnerWrite should runnerDeleted.delete(abs), keeping the delete-outranks-write read without stranding a stale delete record.
